title: Next Permutation
summary: Given an array of integers nums, find the next permutation that is lexicographically greater than the current permutation.
statement: Given an array of integers nums, find the next permutation that is lexicographically greater than the current permutation. If no such permutation exists, rearrange the array into the lowest possible order (i.e., ascending order). The modification must be done in place and should use only constant extra memory.
constraints: 1–100 integers with values 0–100, including possible duplicates.
Rearrange nums into its immediate next lexicographic permutation, wrapping the largest arrangement to the smallest. Modify the input with constant extra memory; no returned list is used.
hints: Change the rightmost position that can be increased, keeping the earlier prefix unchanged.
Find the pivot just before the longest nonincreasing suffix, swap with its smallest larger suffix value, and reverse the suffix.
Scan rightward-to-left for the pivot; scan from the end for a value strictly larger; swap and reverse after the pivot. Without a pivot, reverse all values.
Use strict increase when selecting a successor so equal values do not create the same permutation.
editorial: A nonincreasing suffix is already its largest arrangement. The preceding pivot is therefore the rightmost position that can increase. The rightmost suffix value strictly greater than it is the smallest valid replacement. After swapping, reverse the still-nonincreasing suffix into its minimum order. No pivot means the entire input is maximal and must wrap. The independent oracle enumerates and sorts unique permutations on small inputs.

tests.explanation: Change nums to [1,3,2], the smallest arrangement larger than [1,2,3].
No larger arrangement exists, so wrap to [1,2,3].
